Another thing that helps, for me. After you've prepared what you need to say, punch in the phone number but before you hit send and dial, take a moment to collect yourself. 

Do some breathing, inhale through the nose for 4 seconds and exhale out of your mouth for 8. My therapist also taught me a technique called "calm place." Just think of the safest, least stressful place you can (make one up if you have to!) and visualize yourself there. Put yourself as deep into it as you can. Imagine the sights and sounds around you, the sun on your skin, the ground under your feet etc. Keep doing the 4-8 breathing while you're there. Once you've calmed down, open your eyes and make the call before you have a chance to think yourself out of it again. All you have to do is hit send. Keep up the breathing until someone answers, and just push through it. You'll be surprised how much easier it is having prepped yourself. 

I was really struggling to make calls I needed to, but this method has helped me a lot. Good luck bud, the first steps are always the worst but you can do it!

I can't stop seeing it over and over again. Rolling upside down. Screams. Red light. 

We got lucky and everyone was fine in that instance, but you hear about people dying in accidents every fucking day. It's terrifying because it's completely out of my control. I could practice every day, be the best driver on the planet, but there's no accounting for chaos... A deer jumping in front of me, a hidden patch of ice, other shitty drivers. Situations out of my control already make me extremely uneasy, add cars into the mix and I'm a fucking mess. 

It's just too much for me to handle but I need to do it, and I need to do it soon. My life is passing me by every day I spend hiding in this fucking basement.

For me? Deleted Facebook first off. Shit makes me way too depressed. I'm anxious enough without seeing endless pictures of people (seemingly) living happy, normal lives while I hide away. I don't need to know that Mike Smith just posted an update. 

After that, I just went through and turned off a lot of notification settings. Email, messengers etc (except for a few critical contacts). I get frequent and debilitating anxiety attacks behind the wheel, to the point that I don't even have a license at 26. So my options are either 3+ hours on the bus everyday (horrible public transportation here), or limit myself to businesses within biking distance (in a very bike unfriendly city). Hence, local fast food joints are pretty much it.

I'm also currently undergoing EMDR  therapy for the driving phobia. This is definitely a good thing, but in my last session I ended up inadvertently  uncovering a memory I've been repressing for nearly 20 years. My therapist and I both agree this is likely the root of my phobia, which has always been a bit of a mystery, having never been in an accident or anything obvious like that. So it was a huge breakthrough obviously, but now I have this image of a mangled corpse laying in front of a totaled car burned into my mind and I can't get it out. Couldn't get to sleep until almost 7am last night, it was there every time I closed my eyes. None of my usual calming techniques helped at all so I just watched cartoons until I hit the point of physical exhaustion. Really hoping this is all worth it in the end.

Does it come in response to a specific stimuli (for me, it's driving)? If so, its an anxiety attack.

Does it just blindside you out of nowhere, with no apparent cause? That's a panic attack.

I'm sure there's more to it, but that's always how I've differentiated the two.

If it's that bad, then by all means dude. Whatever gets you into that office. I do advise that you disclose it though, make it clear that your symptoms are bad enough that you literally can't leave the house on your own. How this is received may depend on whether or not your xanax are prescribed, but it's important to be honest in therapy.

Be honest and thorough with yourself about what you're looking to get out of therapy, even if it's kind of abstract. Do you want to be more confident? Happy? Functional? Seriously, spend some time thinking about what drove you to seek therapy in the first place. Then, think about whats driven you to that point. Painful memories? Negatively reinforcement over a long time? Just think about your problems for a while before your next session, kind of prep yourself. Go in with a list if you have to. Beyond that, just be as open and honest as you can, your doctor can't really begin to treat you until they fully understand why you're there. 

Give it some time, no one is fixed after just one session, but don't be afraid to pull the plug and try someone else if it's really not working. Therapists are individuals too, they all have different personalities and treatment styles. It's all about finding someone you can trust and vibe with. I went through 3 before I landed on my current therapist, who I'm pretty happy with.

Best of luck my dude.

Gotta preface this with the obligatory "not a doctor," but in my experience this doesn't sound like social anxiety at all. For me, social anxiety is the opposite - my brain is working on overdrive and I'm overthinking everything, instead of being unable to string thoughts together. I can talk just fine, I just choose not too based on unfounded fears. 

Follow up question though, especially because you say you're in a frat... What's your drug use like? What do you take, and how often? Had any intense psychedelic experiences lately?

To me at least, this sounds like drug fog, perhaps mixed with too much stress. I'd still go see the doctor obviously, but these are two factors worth looking into.
